# dsh-plugin-busy-workspace
**Shows which workspace is working, in the sidebar.**
A DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) Web GUI plugin that highlights running sessions and pins busy workspaces
to the top of the sidebar.
*One list, five phases, ranked by urgency: waiting (amber) first, then running (blue, carrying its s
ubagent chip), then finished-unread (green), then seen — the selected row, in the plugin's own viole
t — and last a run that went quiet (red), marked but deliberately not promoted. The green workspace
is holding four sessions behind the official overflow row: the row that reported the completion is n
o longer on screen, and the header still names the state and still holds its place. Every bar, tint,
ring, badge and chip here is the plugin's own CSS, driven by its own `paint()` over real `data-stat
e` values. The list contents are a fixture and the workspace names are blurred, because a sidebar's
real contents are per-installation; regenerate with `node scripts/capture-screenshots.mjs`.*
## The problem
If you run more than one agent at a time, the `dsh` sidebar becomes a wall of look-alike rows. Every
workspace header renders identically, every session row renders identically, and the only signal th
at something is running is a ten-pixel dot you have to hunt for.
The result is a set of real, recurring failures:
| What happens | What it costs you |
| You cannot tell which workspace has an agent mid-task | You open workspaces one by one to check, o

r you interrupt a session that was already working |
| Busy workspaces drift down the list as you to

uch others | The thing you actually care about is the thing you have to scroll to find |
| A session
finishes and nothing tells you | You wait on a task that already ended, or you miss the moment to r

eview its output |
[该节后续省略]
## What this plugin does
It answers two different questions: **what is moving right now**, and **where did the thing I starte
d go**. Conflating them is what produced the worst defect in its earlier versions — see "a completio
n stays findable" below.
## How it works
The plugin reads `data-state` from the status dot the Harness already renders on every session row.
That attribute is the official contract and carries exactly four values, straight from the Harness's
own `sessionStatuses` / `sessionNode` derivation and in its own priority order: `warning` (waiting
on you, outranking everything) → `ongoing` (running) → `done` (completed, unread) → `idle`.
Those four states cannot express **"I came back for the result"**, so the plugin keeps its own **att
ention phase** on top of them. The only extra information is whether the user has acknowledged the r
ow, and whether the user is currently sitting on it — and neither needs persisting, because the Harn
ess already stores the acknowledgement.
The transitions, which are the whole of `assess()`:

- `warning` → **waiting**; never age-gated, because it is blocking.
- `ongoing` and younger than `st

aleRunMinutes` → **running**; otherwise **interrupted** (marked red, not promoted).
- `done` and you

nger than `unreadHoldMinutes` → **finished (unread)**; older, entirely quiet.
- `done → idle` — whic
h is exactly what opening a session does — → **seen**. While that row is also selected, its dwell cl
ock is restarted on every pass, so reading never loses its place; the `seenHoldMinutes` countdown on
ly begins once the user moves on.
Three selector details are load-bearing:
- **The status read is pinned to the dot's own node.** A row's leading 16px cell renders *either* th
e status dot *or* a `sidebar.session.row.leading` seat contributed by another plugin, so the lookup
requires the primitive's `aria-hidden` marker and restricts the value to the four session states. Wi
thout that, a foreign element carrying a `data-state` (the installer's `error` mark, say) can be mis

read as the session's status. A session row itself never carries `error`.
- **The subagent count com
es from the row's hidden status label**, and the unit is taken from that same label (`子智能体` / `subag
ent(s)`), so the chip is localized by construction rather than by the plugin shipping translations.

, so the chip is localized by construction rather than by the plugin shipping translations.
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility

DeepSeek Harness gates a plugin **itself**, and it does so through
`peerDependencies`, not through `

engines.dsh`: before importing a plugin it
compares every `@deepseek-ai/dsh` / `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*`

peer against the running
runtime version with `semver.satisfies(range, { includePrerelease: true })`

. A
plugin that declares no such peer is not checked at all. So this one declares
one, spelled as on

e branch per release line so that the harness's own check and a
plain semver evaluator agree:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Harness | **0.1.5-rc.1 and later, below 0.3.0** — every release line from 0.1.5 to 0.2.1 is declar
ed. 0.1.0–0.1.4 and 0.3.0+ are refused, loudly, with the profile's `skippedBundles` entry and the `d

sh plugin allow-version …` command to override it deliberately |
| Enforced from | `0.1.7-rc.1` — ea
rlier builds contain no compatibility check at all, so there the declared range is a statement rathe

r than a gate |
| Verified end-to-end | `0.2.0-rc.2` — loaded and observed in a real Web GUI, both h

alves byte-identical to this tree |
| Contract-inspected | the status dot's `data-state` and all sev
en theme tokens are present in `0.1.5-rc.1`, so the floor is a real contract floor and not a guess |

| Verified offline | every declared line — `npm test` needs neither harness nor browser |
| Declare
d, not yet exercised live | `0.1.5-rc.*`, `0.1.6-alpha.*`, `0.1.7-alpha.*` / `-rc.*`, `0.2.0-rc.1`,

`0.2.1-alpha.*` |
| Surface | Web GUI sidebar (`sidebar.workspaces`) |
| Themes | Any theme defining

the standard `--dsw-alias-*` tokens |
| Conflicts | None known. The plugin owns one style element a
nd one settings file, reads no other plugin's state, and registers no UI seat |

The full mechanism, the contract-by-contract dependency table, what each
evidence level does and doe

s not prove, and the procedure for adding a release
line are in **docs/COMPATIBILITY.md**
(中文).

If a harness release changes one of the DOM contracts above, the failure mode is
silence rather than

breakage — the sidebar simply looks stock. The plugin writes
